A lab is only useful once you can get into its nodes. Containerlab gives you several ways in, from a shell on the lab
host to a Python script that logs in to every router. This part tries each one on the routed lab from
[Part 3](../03-topology-file/), then verifies them all.

| Method | Works from | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| SSH by node name | the lab host | everyday work on one router |
| `docker exec` | the lab host | Linux hosts, and routers whose login you have lost |
| `containerlab exec` | the lab host | one command on many nodes at once |
| SSH through a jump host | any machine that can SSH to the lab host | working from your laptop |
| A route to the management network | a machine on the same LAN | using desktop tools such as SecureCRT or Wireshark directly |
| A published port | any machine that can reach the lab host | one service on one node |
| Generated inventories | the lab host | Ansible, Nornir and Python automation |

## Start the lab

Update your copy of the workshop files, then deploy the Part 3 lab:

```bash
cd ~/dynanet-dev && git pull
cd ~/dynanet-dev/clab-workshop/labs/03-topology
containerlab deploy -t routed.clab.yml
```

To recall the lab's layout, open it in the [topology viewer](https://graphs.dynanet.dev/topology?example=routed).
The commands below assume you are in `~/dynanet-dev/clab-workshop/labs/03-topology` unless they say otherwise.

## SSH by node name

Containerlab adds every node to the lab host's `/etc/hosts` as `clab-<lab>-<node>`, so you can use names instead of
addresses:

```bash
ssh clab-routed-srl1
```

You land at the SR Linux prompt without typing a username or password, because Containerlab does two things at deploy
time:

- it writes `/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/clab-routed.conf`, which sets the username (`admin` for SR Linux) and turns off
  host key checks for the lab's nodes, so a redeployed node does not trigger a warning
- it copies the SSH public keys in your `~/.ssh` folder onto the SR Linux nodes

If you have no SSH key, SSH asks for the password instead. To create a key, run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`, then redeploy
with `containerlab deploy -t routed.clab.yml --reconfigure` so the routers get it.

Logins for the kinds used in this workshop:

| Kind | Username | Password |
|---|---|---|
| Nokia SR Linux | `admin` | `NokiaSrl1!` |
| Cisco XRd | `clab` | `clab@123` |
| Arista cEOS | `admin` | `admin` |
| Linux (Alpine) | no SSH server; use `docker exec` | |

## docker exec

Every node is a container, so `docker exec` runs a program inside it. Add `-it` for an interactive session:

| Node | Command | You get |
|---|---|---|
| Linux host | `docker exec -it clab-routed-h1 sh` | a shell (use `bash` on images that have it) |
| Nokia SR Linux | `docker exec -it clab-routed-srl1 sr_cli` | the SR Linux CLI, no login |
| Cisco XRd | `docker exec -it <node> /pkg/bin/xr_cli.sh` | the IOS XR CLI, after the XRd login |
| Arista cEOS | `docker exec -it <node> Cli` | the EOS CLI |

Without `-it` you can run a single command and get its output, which is handy in scripts:

```bash
docker exec clab-routed-h1 ip route
docker exec clab-routed-srl1 sr_cli "show version"
```

## containerlab exec: one command on many nodes

`containerlab exec` runs a command on every node in a lab, or on the nodes that match a label. Containerlab labels
each node with its name (`clab-node-name`) and kind (`clab-node-kind`):

```bash
# both routers
containerlab exec -t routed.clab.yml --label clab-node-kind=nokia_srlinux --cmd "sr_cli show version"

# one host
containerlab exec -t routed.clab.yml --label clab-node-name=h1 --cmd "ip -4 addr show eth1"
```

The output is grouped by node.

## Connect from another machine

The names in `/etc/hosts` and the SSH settings only exist on the lab host. From your laptop you have three options.

### Through a jump host (works anywhere)

SSH can hop through the lab host to a node in one command. The node's name is looked up on the lab host, so names
still work:

```bash
ssh -J you@labhost admin@clab-routed-srl1
```

Replace `you@labhost` with your login on the lab host. You are asked for the lab host password, then the router
password. This works from Linux, macOS and Windows 10 or later (OpenSSH is built in), and only needs SSH access to the
lab host. To make it permanent, add this to `~/.ssh/config` on your laptop:

```
Host clab-*
    ProxyJump you@labhost
```

Then `ssh admin@clab-routed-srl1` works directly from the laptop.

### A route to the management network (same LAN)

Containerlab lets other machines reach the management network through the lab host. Add a route on your laptop,
replacing `192.168.0.201` with the lab host's address:

```bash
# Ubuntu (lasts until reboot)
sudo ip route add 172.20.20.0/24 via 192.168.0.201
```

```powershell
# Windows, in an administrator PowerShell (-p keeps it after a reboot)
route -p add 172.20.20.0 mask 255.255.255.0 192.168.0.201
```

Then connect to the node's management address, for example `ssh admin@172.20.20.11`, or open a SecureCRT session to
it. Use addresses rather than names, since the names only exist on the lab host. The route only works when the laptop
and the lab host are on the same network; across the internet, use the jump host. After a redeploy, a node has a new
host key, so remove the old one with `ssh-keygen -R 172.20.20.11` if SSH warns about it.

### A published port

A node can publish one of its ports on the lab host, like `docker run -p`. Add `ports` to the node in the topology
file:

```yaml
    srl1:
      kind: nokia_srlinux
      ports:
        - 2201:22
```

After a redeploy, `ssh -p 2201 admin@labhost` reaches srl1's SSH server. This suits one service on one node; for many
nodes, the jump host is simpler.

## Use the generated inventories

Containerlab writes inventory files into the lab folder (`clab-routed/`) on every deploy:

| File | Used by |
|---|---|
| `ansible-inventory.yml` | Ansible: nodes grouped by kind, with addresses and the kind's login |
| `nornir-simple-inventory.yml` | Nornir's SimpleInventory |
| `topology-data.json` | your own scripts: every node's name, kind, image and management address, and every link |

Because they are rebuilt on each deploy, they always match the running lab. Here is `show_version.py` from
`labs/04-connect`, which reads `topology-data.json` and logs in to every SR Linux router:

```python
import json
import sys

from netmiko import ConnectHandler

data_file = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "../03-topology/clab-routed/topology-data.json"
with open(data_file) as f:
    nodes = json.load(f)["nodes"]

for name, node in sorted(nodes.items()):
    if node["kind"] != "nokia_srlinux":
        continue
    conn = ConnectHandler(device_type="nokia_srl", host=node["mgmt-ipv4-address"],
                          username="admin", password="NokiaSrl1!")
    output = conn.send_command("show version")
    conn.disconnect()
    version = next((line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in output.splitlines()
                    if line.startswith("Software Version")), "unknown")
    print(f"{name:6} {node['mgmt-ipv4-address']:15} SR Linux {version}")
```

Ubuntu does not let `pip` install into the system Python, so install Netmiko in a virtual environment once:

```bash
sudo apt install -y python3-venv
python3 -m venv ~/clab-venv
~/clab-venv/bin/pip install netmiko
```

Then run the script:

```bash
cd ../04-connect
~/clab-venv/bin/python show_version.py
```

```
srl1   172.20.20.11    SR Linux v26.7.2
srl2   172.20.20.12    SR Linux v26.7.2
```

## Verify

Run each check on the lab host.

| Step | Command | You should see |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Names | `grep clab-routed /etc/hosts` | a line for each of `clab-routed-srl1`, `-srl2`, `-h1` and `-h2` with its 172.20.20.x address (plus a second line each with an IPv6 address on some hosts) |
| 2. SSH by name | `ssh clab-routed-srl1`, then `show version`, then `quit` | the SR Linux prompt with no password (or a password prompt if you have no SSH key), then `Software Version` |
| 3. docker exec | `docker exec clab-routed-h1 hostname` | `h1` |
| 4. containerlab exec | `containerlab exec -t routed.clab.yml --label clab-node-kind=nokia_srlinux --cmd "sr_cli show version"` | a `Software Version` line for each of srl1 and srl2 |
| 5. Inventories | `ls clab-routed/` | `ansible-inventory.yml`, `nornir-simple-inventory.yml` and `topology-data.json` among the files |
| 6. Python | `~/clab-venv/bin/python ../04-connect/show_version.py clab-routed/topology-data.json` | one line each for srl1 and srl2 with the SR Linux version |
| 7. From your laptop | `ssh -J you@labhost admin@clab-routed-srl1` | the SR Linux prompt after both passwords |

Or run steps 1 to 6 at once from `labs/04-connect`. `PYTHON` tells the script which Python has Netmiko:

```bash
cd ../04-connect
PYTHON=~/clab-venv/bin/python ./verify.sh
```

```
Checking connection methods on lab routed
  PASS  /etc/hosts has entries for all 4 nodes
  PASS  docker exec opens a shell on h1
  PASS  docker exec runs the SR Linux CLI on srl1
  PASS  containerlab exec ran on both routers
  PASS  ssh clab-routed-srl1 logs in with your SSH key
  PASS  lab folder has ansible-inventory.yml
  PASS  lab folder has nornir-simple-inventory.yml
  PASS  lab folder has topology-data.json
  PASS  show_version.py reached both routers

All checks passed.
```

`SKIP` means a check could not run on your setup, such as having no SSH key or no Netmiko; it is not a failure. Step 7
runs on your laptop, so the script cannot check it.

## Remove the lab

```bash
cd ~/dynanet-dev/clab-workshop/labs/03-topology
containerlab destroy -t routed.clab.yml
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ssh clab-routed-srl1` asks for a password | You had no SSH key when the lab was deployed. Create one with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` and redeploy with `--reconfigure`, or type the password |
| `Could not resolve hostname clab-routed-srl1` on your laptop | Names only exist on the lab host. Use the jump host, or the management address with a route |
| SSH from the laptop to 172.20.20.x times out | Check the route (`ip route` or `route print`), that the laptop is on the lab host's LAN, and that the lab is running |
| `WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED` | The node was redeployed and has a new key. Run `ssh-keygen -R <address>` and connect again |
| `docker exec ... xr_cli.sh` prints a terminal error | Add `-it`; the XRd CLI needs an interactive terminal |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'netmiko'` | Run the script with the virtual environment's Python: `~/clab-venv/bin/python` |
